title: Uber Builds GitFarm to Run Git Operations as a Service for Large-Scale Monorepos
gist: Uber built GitFarm, a centralized gRPC-based Git-as-a-Service that replaces local repo clones with pooled, pre-warmed checkouts, cutting client-side compute/memory by over 80% and checkout time from 10-15 minutes to under 500ms across its Go/Java/Python/Web/Android/iOS monorepos.

themes.theme: Scale of the problem GitFarm solves

insights.claim: Uber's automation systems invoke Git millions of times per day across its monorepos, and previously each service maintained its own full repository checkout to read files, validate changes, and calculate merge bases.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: At hyperscaler scale, naive per-service Git cloning becomes a direct infrastructure cost center, not just a developer-experience annoyance -- a pattern likely repeating at other large monorepo shops (Google, Meta, Microsoft).
insights.locator: Uber's automation systems invoke Git millions of times per day

insights.claim: Cloning Uber's Go monorepo alone took roughly 15 minutes and required about six CPU cores, 32 GB of memory, and more than 40 GB of disk per instance before GitFarm.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Quantifies the per-clone compute tax that centralized Git services eliminate -- a concrete capex/efficiency case study for platform teams evaluating similar investments.
insights.locator: Cloning Uber's Go monorepo takes roughly 15 minutes

insights.claim: GitFarm is not a source control system but a centralized Git client exposed via a high-performance gRPC API: a Gateway authenticates and authorizes requests before routing them to backend clusters that run commands in isolated, ephemeral sandboxes.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Separates the source-of-truth layer from the execution layer, letting Uber scale Git compute independently of the underlying SCM (GitHub/GitLab-class systems).
insights.locator: It is not a source control management system

insights.claim: GitFarm maintains bare repository clones synchronized via push-based updates and periodic fetches, plus pools of pre-warmed repository checkouts and sandbox containers, so a request can mount an existing checkout instead of cloning from scratch -- delivering full Git checkouts in under 500 milliseconds versus historical 10-15 minute cold starts.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A ~1000x-2000x reduction in checkout latency demonstrates how much idle capacity is wasted by treating every automated job as a fresh clone -- a reusable pooling pattern for any org running CI/CD or agent workloads against large repos.
insights.locator: Uber Engineering said in a LinkedIn post

insights.claim: GitFarm supports multi-command workflows through bidirectional gRPC streaming sessions, letting clients fetch a branch, calculate a merge base, and push a derived reference sequentially against the same checkout without reinitializing repository state each time.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Session-based Git operations avoid redundant state rebuilding, a meaningful latency and cost lever for any automation that chains multiple Git commands.

insights.claim: A code ownership service eliminated local checkouts across six hosts after adopting GitFarm, cutting CPU consumption from more than 70 cores to 16, memory from 400 GB to 32 GB, and startup time from 15-20 minutes to under one minute.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A ~4x CPU and ~12x memory reduction on a single internal service quantifies the capex savings other teams inside Uber (and comparable orgs) could realize by migrating off local clones.
insights.locator: a code ownership service eliminated local checkouts

insights.claim: A compliance auditing service processing 10,000-20,000 events per hour across 9,000 repositories cut median latency from 110-160 seconds on Buildkite to 20-30 seconds with GitFarm by removing scheduling, workspace initialization, and repository synchronization overhead.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A roughly 5x latency improvement on a high-volume compliance workload shows GitFarm's benefit extends beyond raw resource savings into materially faster audit/compliance turnaround.
insights.locator: A compliance auditing service processing 10,000 to 20,000 events

themes.theme: Forward-looking: coding agents as a Git-infrastructure driver

insights.claim: Uber engineer Ashish Verma noted that AI coding agents repeatedly and concurrently search, branch, diff, experiment, retry, and validate changes, which could substantially increase Git infrastructure load beyond typical human developer usage patterns.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: As coding agents scale inside enterprises, centralized, low-latency Git-as-a-Service infrastructure like GitFarm becomes a prerequisite rather than an optimization -- a forward signal for demand in developer-platform tooling (source control, CI, sandboxing).
insights.locator: Ashish Verma noted on LinkedIn that agents repeatedly search

insights.claim: GitFarm has been running in production since early 2025, with a roadmap covering streaming Git output, sparse checkouts, bare workspaces, longer-lived sessions, repository mirroring, and SubmitQueue integration.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Over a year of production hardening before public disclosure, plus an active roadmap, signals GitFarm is core infrastructure investment rather than a one-off optimization project.
